newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut governor fined over concert tickets.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut governor fined over concert tickets.

text.p: A Connecticut ethics panel on Friday fined Republican Gov. John Rowland a maximum $2,000 for accepting free concert tickets six times in the last two years.

Rowland attended concerts at the Meadows Music Theatre in Hartford with tickets purchased by members of his staff or by a businessman whose firm does business with the state, Ethics Commission Executive Director Alan Plofsky said.
"That is a violation of the law," Plofsky told Reuters.

"When the governor and his friends and colleagues arrived at the Meadows ... their seats were routinely upgraded from the normal $40 or $50 seat to a luxury box seat that has a value of $160," Plofsky said.
"Each time that happened, there was also a violation."
Rowland, 39, was the first governor in the state's history to be fined for an ethics violation, Plofsky said.
In addition to the $2,000 fine, Rowland also agreed to pay $1,900 to charity.
Rowland told a news conference that he had to sit in the upgraded seats for "security reasons."
Five members of his staff also agreed to pay about $1,900 to charity for sitting in luxury box seats after they had paid for non-box seats, Plofsky said.
The concerts attended by Rowland were by James Taylor, Carly Simon, Reba McEntire, the Eagles, Celine Dion and Jimmy Buffett.
Rowland, Connecticut's first Republican governor in 20 years, was elected in 1994.
